FACT-5.gloss: The top level (level 4) has a square footage of 16

RULE-1.gloss: If level n of x's sandcastle has square footage s, level m is directly below level n, and s divided by 2 equals t, then level m has square footage t
RULE-1.verify_reason: The problem states the upper level has half the square footage of the level below it, so a lower level should have twice (not half) the square footage of the level above it; dividing by 2 inverts the relationship.

RULE-2.gloss: If x's sandcastle has n levels with square footages s1, s2, s3, s4 for levels 1,2,3,4 respectively, the sum of those square footages is sum, and sum divided by n equals avg, then the average square footage of a level of x's sandcastle is avg
RULE-2.formula: ∀x∀n∀s1∀s2∀s3∀s4∀sum∀avg (Levels(x,n) ∧ SquareFootage(x,1,s1) ∧ SquareFootage(x,2,s2) ∧ SquareFootage(x,3,s3) ∧ SquareFootage(x,4,s4) ∧ Sum(s1,s2,s3,s4,sum) ∧ Quotient(sum,n,avg) → Average(x,avg))
